parts.text:
Meeting: Customer feedback and notifications – Bakery Brasa (fictional data)
Date: 2026-10-12
Recording part: 1 of 1 (00:00–16:30)
Attendees: Paula Vega (Marketing, stakeholder), Julián Mora (Business analyst), Andrés Gil (Developer), Sofía Rojas (QA)

[00:00:18] Julián: Paula, you asked for this meeting. Tell us what you are looking for.
[00:00:30] Paula: I do not know what customers think of us after they receive the order. Right now I only know when somebody complains on Instagram, and by then it is too late.
[00:01:10] Julián: So you would like to ask them directly.
[00:01:14] Paula: Yes. Something short, after the order arrives. Stars, one to five, and a space to write if they want.
[00:02:00] Sofía: Every order, or only some?
[00:02:08] Paula: Every delivered order, but only once per order of course. And not too fast, maybe a few hours later, so they have eaten the bread.
[00:02:40] Andrés: How do they receive it, email or in the app?
[00:02:50] Paula: I think email. Although... honestly I am not sure. If we also notify them when the order is ready for pickup, maybe it should be the same channel. I need to ask my team.
[00:03:30] Julián: Then we leave the channel open and you come back to us.
[00:03:36] Paula: Yes.
[00:04:20] Paula: Will the reviews be public on the website?
[00:04:28] Julián: Do you want that?
[00:04:33] Paula: No, not now. Private. First I want to read them and see what they say.
[00:06:10] Sofía: Can I bring something up? In QA I noticed the confirmation emails show the pickup time two hours off. A customer picks 10:00 and the email says 08:00.
[00:06:25] Andrés: That sounds like a time zone problem in the email template. I did not know.
[00:06:35] Paula: Oh, that is serious, people arrive at the wrong time. Please fix that first, before anything new.
[00:06:50] Julián: So the time zone problem goes first, the feedback after.
[00:07:00] Paula: Yes. The feedback I would like before the holiday campaign starts, early November.
[00:09:30] Paula: One more idea, a loyalty program with points. But I have no details yet, it is just an idea.
[00:09:42] Julián: Then we do not write anything down now. When you have details we talk.
[00:09:48] Paula: Fine.

meeting.goals: Paula Vega asked for the meeting to learn what customers think after they receive an order, and to agree what a customer feedback request should look like.
topics: Paula only learns about complaints from Instagram, too late. She wants a short request after the order arrives: one to five stars and an optional comment.
Every delivered order, once per order, a few hours after delivery so customers have eaten the bread.
Email is likely, but it may need to match the channel for ready-for-pickup notifications. Undecided; Paula will ask her team.
Reviews stay private for now. Paula wants to read them before deciding anything public.
Pickup time wrong in confirmation emails
QA saw the confirmation email show the pickup time two hours off (10:00 picked, 08:00 shown). Andrés suspects a time zone problem in the email template.
The time zone problem is fixed first, the feedback request after. Paula wants the feedback before the holiday campaign starts in early November.
Only an idea with no details. Nothing is written down until Paula has details.
actions: **Unassigned:** Fix the pickup time shown in confirmation emails (high).
**Unassigned:** Send customers a feedback request after a delivered order (medium).
**Paula Vega:** Ask her team which channel the feedback request uses and come back to the team.
decisions: The pickup time bug in confirmation emails is fixed before the feedback request.
The feedback request is sent for every delivered order, once per order, a few hours after delivery.
Customers rate from one to five stars and can add a comment.
Feedback is private for now; it is not shown on the website.
The feedback request is wanted before the holiday campaign starts in early November.

items.title: Fix the pickup time shown in confirmation emails
items.desc: The confirmation email shows the pickup time two hours earlier than the customer chose: a customer picks 10:00 and the email says 08:00. Customers could arrive at the wrong time. Found in QA; a time zone problem in the email template is suspected but not confirmed.

items.title: Ask customers for feedback after a delivered order
items.desc: After an order is delivered, the customer gets a short request to rate the order from one to five stars and optionally write a comment.
